q: How does EcoVadis grade how reliable my carbon figures are?
title: How EcoVadis grades your carbon figures
short: Each carbon figure you report gets one of four levels: Low, Medium, High or Third-Party Verified. EcoVadis checks evidence first, then accounting rigor, then plausibility against industry benchmarks. High needs documented, GHG Protocol-aligned figures; only figures checked by an independent auditor reach the top level.
audience: Indian MSME suppliers reporting emissions to buyers through EcoVadis

ol: Evidence: is the figure backed by a document, such as an inventory report, a CDP response or a sustainability report?
Rigor: was it calculated in line with the GHG Protocol, and has it been verified by a third party?
Plausibility: does it look realistic against benchmarks for your industry, or does it stand out as a statistical outlier?

sections.h: What each level tells your buyer
ul: Third-Party Verified: checked by an independent auditor. Recommended for external reporting and Scope 3.
High: documented and GHG Protocol-aligned. Also recommended for external reporting and Scope 3, so a buyer can use it in place of an industry average.
Medium: partly follows good practice. Fit for internal tracking only.
Low: not enough evidence, or fails the statistical checks. Not for external reporting; needs correction.
EcoVadis notes it identifies verified data but does not act as the auditor.

sections.h: Why an Indian supplier's figure stalls at Low or Medium
ul: A total with no inventory document behind it.
No year, boundary or method stated, so rigor cannot be judged.
Factors not named. Say which grid factor and which fuel factors you used, and where they come from.
Generator diesel or a second site left out, so the total looks low for your industry and output.
Scope 2 given as one number. Since May 2026 EcoVadis asks for location-based and market-based separately, and grades the reliability of each.

sections.h: Moving a figure from Medium to High
ol: Write a short inventory report: year, sites covered, method (GHG Protocol), each fuel and electricity line with quantity, factor and source.
Keep the bills behind every line, in case a reviewer asks.
Add a sentence explaining anything unusual, such as a new furnace or a month of shutdown, so the plausibility check has context.
For Third-Party Verified, have the inventory verified by an independent body and upload the statement.

example.title: Inventory lines that pass evidence and rigor
lines: Grid electricity: 9,00,000 kWh x 0.675 kg CO2/kWh (CEA, FY 2025-26) = 607.5 t CO2.
Diesel for generators: 40,000 L x 2.645 kg/L (IPCC) = 105.8 t CO2.
Piped natural gas: 3,00,000 scm x 2.05 kg/scm = 615.0 t CO2.
Total Scope 1 and 2: 1,328.3 t CO2, with 24 monthly power bills, 18 diesel invoices and 12 gas bills behind it.
example.note: Quantities are invented; factors are the ones Senseible applies.

senseible: Senseible's records give the first two checks what they look for: each figure tied to its bill, with the factor and its source. Its Verified status means its rule checks passed; it is not independent verification, so on its own it cannot earn EcoVadis's Third-Party Verified level.
